data.one_liner: Encapsulates TabController, TabBar and TabBarView into a single customizable Widget.
data.what_it_does: Combines a TabController, TabBar, and TabBarView into one easy-to-use widget. It allows you to customize tab bar positions (top, bottom, left, right), alignment, appearance, and physics without manually managing the internal tab controller ecosystem.
use_when: You want to combine tabs and views into a single container-friendly widget without boilerplate.
You need custom tab bar positions like left, right, or bottom relative to the views.
You need to programmatically change tabs using a GlobalKey.
avoid_when: You require complex custom Scaffold-level nested navigation where standard DefaultTabController is preferred.
strengths: Simplifies working with TabBar and TabBarView by encapsulating them into one widget.
Supports flexible tab bar positioning (top, bottom, left, right) and alignment.
Exposes state methods like animateTo(), next(), and previous() for external control.
weaknesses: Limited to tab-based interfaces and associated properties.
data.minimal_example:
Container(
  width: 200,
  height: 300,
  child: ContainedTabBarView(
    tabs: [
      Text('First'),
      Text('Second'),
    ],
    views: [
      Container(color: Colors.red),
      Container(color: Colors.green)
    ],
    onChange: (index) => print(index),
  ),
)
